**Formula 1 Grand Prix that have taken place in Asia or the Middle East (including trans‑continental venues that are generally classified as Asian)**  

| # | Grand Prix (most recent name) | Country / Region | Circuit (city) | Years run in F1* | Driver with the most wins at that circuit (wins) |
|---|------------------------------|------------------|----------------|------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Bahrain Grand Prix** | Bahrain (Middle East) | **Bahrain International Circuit** – Sakhir | 2004‑2019, 2021‑2024 (2020 cancelled) | **Sebastian Vettel** – 5 wins (2011, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2017) |
| 2 | **Saudi Arabian Grand Prix** | Saudi Arabia (Middle East) | **Jeddah Corniche Circuit** – Jeddah | 2021‑2024 (2022‑2023 held twice a year) | **Max Verstappen** – 3 wins (2022, 2023, 2024) |
| 3 | **Qatar Grand Prix** | Qatar (Middle East) | **Lusail International Circuit** – Lusail | 2021 (canceled) – 2022‑2024 | **Max Verstappen** – 3 wins (2022, 2023, 2024) |
| 4 | **Abu Dhabi Grand Prix** | United Arab Emirates (Middle East) | **Yas Marina Circuit** – Abu Dhabi | 2009‑2024 (2020 cancelled) | **Lewis Hamilton** – 5 wins (2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019) |
| 5 | **Singapore Grand Prix** | Singapore (Southeast Asia) | **Marina Bay Street Circuit** – Singapore | 2008‑2019, 2022‑2024 (2020‑2021 cancelled) | **Sebastian Vettel** – 3 wins (2011‑2013) |
| 6 | **Japanese Grand Prix** | Japan (East Asia) | **Suzuka International Racing Course** – Suzuka | 1987‑2006, 2009‑2024 (2007‑2008 held at Fuji) | **Lewis Hamilton** – 6 wins (2007, 2009, 2012, 2015, 2017, 2018) |
| 7 | **Chinese Grand Prix** | China (East Asia) | **Shanghai International Circuit** – Shanghai | 2004‑2008, 2014‑2019, 2021‑2024 (2020‑2022 cancelled) | **Lewis Hamilton** – 3 wins (2014, 2015, 2017) |
| 8 | **Malaysian Grand Prix** | Malaysia (Southeast Asia) | **Sepang International Circuit** – Sepang | 1999‑2017 (except 2009) | **Michael Schumacher** – 3 wins (2001, 2002, 2004) |
| 9 | **Indian Grand Prix** | India (South Asia) | **Buddh International Circuit** – Greater Noida | 2011‑2013 | **Sebastian Vettel** – 3 wins (2011‑2013) |
|10| **Korean Grand Prix** | South Korea (East Asia) | **Korea International Circuit** – Yeongam | 2010‑2013 | **Sebastian Vettel** – 3 wins (2011‑2013) |
|11| **Azerbaijan Grand Prix** | Azerbaijan (Caucasus, trans‑continental) | **Baku City Circuit** – Baku | 2016‑2024 (2020 cancelled) | **Lewis Hamilton** – 2 wins (2018, 2021) – tied with Max Verstappen (2022, 2023) |
|12| **Turkish Grand Prix** | Turkey (trans‑continental) | **Istanbul Park** – Tuzla (Istanbul) | 2005‑2011, 2021‑2022 | **Michael Schumacher** – 2 wins (2005, 2006) – tied with Felipe Massa (2007, 2011) |

\* **Years run** counts only seasons in which the race actually took place; years where the event was scheduled but cancelled (e.g., 2020‑2022 COVID‑related cancellations) are omitted.

---

### How the “most‑wins” driver was determined
* The count includes **only** races held on the *current* Grand‑Prix circuit (e.g., Suzuka for the Japanese GP, not the temporary Fuji layout used in 2007‑2008).  
* If two drivers share the highest number of victories on a circuit, the table notes the tie.  
* Data are current through the end of the **2024 F1 season** (the most recent completed season at the time of writing).  

---

### Quick reference (just the drivers)

| Grand Prix | Driver with most wins |
|------------|-----------------------|
| Bahrain | Sebastian Vettel (5) |
| Saudi Arabia | Max Verstappen (3) |
| Qatar | Max Verstappen (3) |
| Abu Dhabi | Lewis Hamilton (5) |
| Singapore | Sebastian Vettel (3) |
| Japan (Suzuka) | Lewis Hamilton (6) |
| China | Lewis Hamilton (3) |
| Malaysia | Michael Schumacher (3) |
| India | Sebastian Vettel (3) |
| Korea | Sebastian Vettel (3) |
| Azerbaijan | Lewis Hamilton = Max Verstappen (2 each) |
| Turkey | Michael Schumacher = Felipe Massa (2 each) |

These are the Asian and Middle‑Eastern venues that have hosted a Formula 1 Grand Prix and the drivers who have been most successful at each of them. If you need more detailed statistics (e.g., exact race dates, podium finishers, or win‑percentage), just let me know!
